plain.1: A loop that electricity can travel round. If the loop is broken, nothing moves.
plain.3: A closed conducting path from the battery's + terminal, through components, back to its − terminal.

plain.1: The push. How hard the battery shoves electricity round the loop. Measured in volts (V).
plain.2: The electrical push between two points, in volts (V). A bigger voltage pushes more current through the same resistance.
plain.4: Potential difference between two points: energy per unit charge, in volts (V).

plain.1: The flow. How much electricity is moving past a point each second. Measured in amps (A).
plain.2: The flow of charge, in amps (A). 1000 milliamps (mA) make 1 amp.
plain.4: Rate of flow of charge, I = ΔQ/Δt, in amps (A).

plain.1: The squeeze. How hard a part makes it for electricity to get through. Measured in ohms (Ω).
plain.2: How much a part opposes the current, in ohms (Ω). More resistance means less current for the same voltage.

plain.1: Your power supply. Its + side pushes electricity out and its − side takes it back in.
A gap you can open and close. Closed = the loop is complete and electricity flows. Open = the loop is broken.
A part that glows when electricity flows through it. Too much and it pops.
A tiny light that is very fussy. Too much flow and it retires early. It only works one way round.
plain.3: Light-emitting diode. Conducts one way only, and drops a fixed forward voltage (about 2 V for red).

plain.1: A part whose job is to squeeze the flow, so other parts stay safe.
A resistor you can slide. More squeeze, less flow, dimmer bulb.
plain.3: A variable resistor (potentiometer used as a rheostat).

plain.1: Parts one after another in a single loop. Same flow through all of them.
Parts side by side, on separate paths. Each path gets the full push.
How hungry a part is: how fast it uses up energy. Measured in watts (W).
plain.3: Rate of energy transfer, P = VI, in watts (W).

plain.1: A thousandth of an amp. 1000 mA = 1 A. Small parts use small flows, so we use mA.
How much a battery holds. Measured in milliamp-hours (mAh). Bigger lasts longer.
A tool that shows the push (volts) or the flow (amps) at a part. In the workshop, tap a part and read the panel.
